26 A transverse water wave has a frequency of 15 Hz, a wavelength of 0.12 m and an amplitude of
4.0 mm.
P is a water particle that is initially at the peak of the wave, as shown.
P
What is the total vertical distance travelled by P in a time of 0.5 s?
A
30 mm
B
60 mm
C
120 mm
D
900 mm

hints: Notice P is a water particle, so it only oscillates vertically about its mean position and does not travel with the $0.12 \text{ m}$ wavelength.
Connect the $15 \text{ Hz}$ frequency to the number of vertical oscillations in $0.5 \text{ s}$ using $N = f \times t$.
Connect the $4.0 \text{ mm}$ amplitude to distance per full oscillation: peak to mean to trough to mean to peak is four amplitudes.
walkthrough: Identify the motion: P oscillates vertically with frequency $f = 15 \text{ Hz}$ and amplitude $a = 4.0 \text{ mm}$. The $0.12 \text{ m}$ wavelength controls wave speed, not the particle path.
Find the number of oscillations in $0.5 \text{ s}$ using $N = f t$. Substituting gives $N = 15 \times 0.5 = 7.5$ oscillations.
Find the vertical path in one full oscillation. From peak down to trough is $2a$ and back up to peak is another $2a$, so distance per cycle $= 4a = 4 \times 4.0 \text{ mm} = 16 \text{ mm}$.
Multiply cycles by distance per cycle: total distance $= N \times 4a = 7.5 \times 16 \text{ mm} = 120 \text{ mm}$.

Starting at the peak does not change the total path because each complete oscillation has the same length, and the final half oscillation also contributes $2 \times 4.0 \text{ mm}$ per half cycle. This is option C

A.explanation: Too small. $30 \text{ mm}$ is $7.5 \times 4.0 \text{ mm}$, which counts only one amplitude per oscillation instead of the full up-and-down path.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 2. $60 \text{ mm}$ is $7.5 \times 8.0 \text{ mm}$, which counts only peak-to-trough distance per oscillation.

C.explanation: Correct. $7.5$ oscillations each require $4 \times 4.0 \text{ mm} = 16 \text{ mm}$ of vertical path, giving $120 \text{ mm}$.

D.explanation: Incorrect. $900 \text{ mm}$ is the horizontal distance the wave pattern travels in $0.5 \text{ s}$, not the vertical distance moved by particle P.
